'''''Dactylorhiza elata''''', the '''robust marsh orchid''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Orchidaceae, [[native plant|native]] to the western [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean]] region ([[France]] (including [[Corsica]]), [[Sardinia]], [[Spain]], [[Portugal]], [[Algeria]], [[Morocco]] and [[Tunisia]]).<ref name="WCSP">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=55251 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>Castroviejo, S. & al. (eds.) (2005). Flora Iberica 21: 1-366. Real Jardín Botánico, CSIC, Madrid.</ref><ref>Baumann, B. & Baumann, H. (2005). Beiträge zur Kenntnis der Orchideenflora Nordwestafrikas. Journal Europäischer Orchideen 37: 915-938.</ref><ref>Vázquez Pardo, F.M. (2009). Revisión de la familia Orchidaceae en Extremadura (España). Folia Botanica Extremadurensis 3: 1-367.</ref><ref>Dobignard, D. & Chatelain, C. (2010). Index synonymique de la flore d'Afrique du nord 1: 1-455. Éditions des conservatoire et jardin botaniques, Genève.</ref>

''Dactylorhiza elata'' is a [[tuber]]ous [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|50|cm|0|abbr=on}}, and producing dense {{convert|20|cm|0|abbr=on}} spikes of purple flowers in spring.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Dactylorhiza elata''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5285/Dactylorhiza-elata/Details | access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> (confirmed 2017).<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 27 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 24 January 2018}}</ref>

==Subspecies==
Many names have been proposed for subspecies, varieties, subvarieties and forms of the species. As of June 2014, the following are recognized:<ref name="WCSP"/>

*''Dactylorhiza elata'' subsp. ''elata'' - Spain, North Africa
*''Dactylorhiza elata'' subsp. ''sesquipedalis'' <small>(Willd.) Soó</small> - France, Spain, Portugal, Sardinia
